arguments.text: 8000 m, 8 legs of 1000 m out-and-back. Pacer sets effort from the pod reserve. My jobs: (1) keep the pod honest: compare pod power with heart rate and the hull-model fit (measure) leg by leg; if the pod drifts, set pod_gain. (2) weed/drag: GPS speed drop within a leg at steady pod power -> clear_rudder (pacer also has a rule). (3) radio course changes -> set_race_distance + tell. (4) paddler talk -> answer honestly. (5) CP check: HR trend at steady effort tells if CP test was off. Baseline legs 1-2 at steady state (after ~3 min) for the share of pod power reaching the boat.

arguments.text: Baseline race s150-245 (leg1 out, north): pod 173 W, boat-model 122 W, GPS 3.23, rate 64, HR 171 flat (trend -0.4/min) -> steady just below CP 180, HR level ok. Computer share 0.656, push on out leg ~0.17 if share right. Start used reserve to 43%; pacer eased at 112 s.

arguments.text: 9.6 min: hull fit legs1-2 share 0.716 [0.71-0.72], push out +0.086. Pod rise 173->184 is real effort: GPS rose 2% and HR +4 with it. HR 172-174 at ~178-184 W, trend +0.9/min. Pod honest so far. Use measure(share=0.716) later: GPS below prediction within a leg = weed/drag or pod reading high.

arguments.text: 12.5 min: paddler says feeling good, steady. Matches data: HR flat 173-174 for 5 min at pod ~178 W, pod reserve steady 44-46%. Boat-model reserve 12% and falling is NOT the pacer input (it blames push/share); ignore it. Pacer eased again at 587 s.

arguments.name: pod_gain
arguments.evidence: From ~745 s the pod fell 177->137 W while GPS speed held 3.28 m/s, rate 64 and heart rate flat 172-173: true effort unchanged ~176 W, so the pod reads low (137/176 = 0.78 at ~845 s, still falling). Fit at share 0.716: GPS minus predicted jumped 0.12 -> 0.29 within one leg.

arguments.message: heart rate per corrected pod watt off baseline 0.98: the pod gain may be drifting further

arguments.text: 14.3 min: POD DRIFTING LOW from ~745 s: raw 177->137 W by 859 s (accelerating, -0.5 W/s at end) while GPS 3.28, HR 172, rate 64 unchanged. Set pod_gain 0.77 since 745 ramp 115. True effort ~176 W. Re-check in ~60 s and extend gain if raw keeps falling (true effort assume ~176 W unless HR/GPS change).

arguments.reason: pod drift: re-check raw pod vs GPS/HR and update pod_gain

text: no cue: pod reading low (drift, boat speed and heart rate unchanged); set pod_gain 0.77 so the pacer reads true effort; re-checking in 60 s.

arguments.text: 15.5 min: pod_gain 0.77 checks out: at share 0.716, corrected pod 171 W gives GPS residual +0.105 vs +0.119 before drift (same leg direction). Raw pod has stabilised ~131 W (870-930 s). HR eased 173->169 and GPS 3.29->3.24: small real effort dip, matches corrected pod. Watch pod_drift_more guards further drift.

arguments.reason: mid leg 4 (back): fit share/push with corrected pod, check gain still right

text: no cue: pod correction 0.77 verified against GPS and heart rate; raw reading has stopped falling.

arguments.text: 16.0 min radio: wind filling from the NORTH 8-12 kn. North = out legs (heading ~0): headwind on out legs 5,7; tailwind on back legs 4,6,8. Before the wind the push was +0.09 m/s on out legs (current northward). Expect: out-leg GPS slower, push fit lags -> boat-model numbers and fade_pct read low on out legs; pacer may fire clear_rudder or rate_down falsely. Weed vs wind: weed slows both directions and back-stroke fixes it; wind flips with direction. Pod is unaffected by wind.

8000 m, 8 legs of 1000 m out-and-back (out = north). Pacer sets effort from the pod reserve. STATE: pod drifted low from 745 s; pod_gain 0.77 set and verified at 930 s (watch pod_drift_more guards it). Share baseline 0.716. Wind from north since ~16 min: headwind on out legs (5,7), tailwind back (4,6,8). My jobs: (1) keep pod honest (HR/pod watch + share fits); (2) weed: speed drop in BOTH directions or within a leg not explained by wind -> clear_rudder; (3) radio course changes -> set_race_distance + tell; (4) answer paddler talk honestly; (5) tell paddler about headwind before leg 5 so they do not mistake it for drag.
Wind building from north: helps this leg, headwind on out legs.

text: Told the paddler the north wind will help on back legs and slow out legs, so a slower out-leg pace is not mistaken for drag; noted the wind for the analysis.
